questions.question: How do I stop a search parameter from being longer than 50 characters?
questions.answer: Wrap its type in Annotated and put Query(max_length=50) inside.

evidence.quote: add Query inside of Annotated, and set the parameter max_length to 50

questions.question: How do I send my app's traces to my own monitoring collector?
questions.answer: Install fastapi[standard] and set FASTAPI_OTEL_AUTO_CONFIGURE=true, OTEL_SERVICE_NAME and OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT.

evidence.quote: FASTAPI_OTEL_AUTO_CONFIGURE=true enables FastAPI's automatic exporter setup.

questions.notes: Added in 0.142.0 (Sept 2026), after qwen3 was trained: the model alone cannot know it.

questions.question: In my tests, how do I call an endpoint but swap its database dependency for a fake one?
questions.answer: Call it through TestClient(app), and put the fake in app.dependency_overrides with the real dependency as the key.

evidence.quote: Create a TestClient by passing your FastAPI application to it.
To override a dependency for testing, you put as a key the original dependency (a function), and as the value, your dependency override (another function).

questions.notes: Two pages: how to call the app in a test, and how to swap a dependency.

questions.answer: The docs do not cover rate limiting.

questions.question: How do I stream server-sent events?
questions.answer: Use yield in the path operation and set response_class=EventSourceResponse.

evidence.quote: To stream SSE with FastAPI, use yield in your path operation function and set response_class=EventSourceResponse.

questions.notes: Added in 0.135.0 (March 2026), after qwen3 was trained: the model alone cannot know it.

questions.question: How do I serve my built frontend?
questions.answer: Call app.frontend() with the build directory, for example dist.

evidence.quote: You can serve static frontend apps with app.frontend() (or router.frontend()).

questions.notes: Added in 0.138.0 (June 2026), after qwen3 was trained: the model alone cannot know it.

questions.question: How do I handle an unchecked checkbox?
questions.answer: Declare a boolean form field with a default of False. An omitted checkbox arrives as False.

evidence.quote: Declare a boolean form parameter with a default of False to receive False when unchecked

questions.notes: Added in 0.147.0 (Oct 2026), after qwen3 was trained: the model alone cannot know it.

questions.question: Why reject JSON with no content type?
questions.answer: FastAPI requires a Content-Type such as application/json before it parses a body as JSON.

evidence.quote: JSON requests must include a valid Content-Type header (e.g. application/json) in order for the body to be parsed as JSON.

questions.notes: Added in 0.132.0 (Feb 2026), after qwen3 was trained: the model alone cannot know it.

questions.question: How do I deploy to FastAPI Cloud?
questions.answer: Run uv run fastapi deploy. The CLI deploys the app and opens a browser if you are not logged in.

evidence.quote: You can deploy your FastAPI app to FastAPI Cloud with just one command.

questions.notes: fastapi deploy added in 0.116.0 (July 2025). The model alone cannot know it.

questions.question: How do I turn off the docs?
questions.answer: Set the environment variable OPENAPI_URL to an empty string.

evidence.quote: you could disable OpenAPI (including the UI docs) by setting the environment variable OPENAPI_URL to the empty string

questions.question: How do I run code after responding?
questions.answer: Take a BackgroundTasks parameter and pass the function to add_task().

evidence.quote: pass your task function to the background tasks object with the method .add_task()

questions.question: How do I allow requests from another site?
questions.answer: Add CORSMiddleware and put the other site in allow_origins.

evidence.quote: You can configure it in your FastAPI application using the CORSMiddleware.

questions.question: How do I run startup code in tests?
questions.answer: Put the startup code in a lifespan function, and open TestClient inside a with block so lifespan runs.

evidence.quote: You can define this startup and shutdown logic using the lifespan parameter of the FastAPI app
When you need lifespan to run in your tests, you can use the TestClient with a with statement

questions.notes: Two pages: how to declare lifespan, and how to make TestClient run it.

questions.question: How do I write and test a websocket?
questions.answer: Declare a websocket route that awaits and sends messages, then connect to it with TestClient inside a with block.

evidence.quote: In your WebSocket route you can await for messages and send messages.
You can use the same TestClient to test WebSockets.

questions.notes: Two pages: how to write the route, and how to connect to it in a test.
